assignment.title: Practical Assignment — Listen, Connect, Influence
assignment.description:
Your mission: Demonstrate that you can listen to understand, hold an engaging conversation, adapt to another person's communication style, and communicate an idea clearly enough to influence how someone thinks or acts.

This is not a written assignment. You must demonstrate your communication skills through real conversations and a persuasive speech.

You may submit your work as video recordings, audio recordings, or a combination of both. You do not have to appear on camera. What matters is that your recordings clearly demonstrate your communication skills.
assignment.instructions:
PART 1: THE CONVERSATION CHALLENGE

Find someone you can have a genuine conversation with. It could be a friend, classmate, sibling, colleague, or someone you know.

Have a real conversation lasting approximately 5-10 minutes.

Your objective is to understand the person better than you did before the conversation.

BEFORE YOU BEGIN RECORDING

Start your recording by introducing yourself so that the examiner can identify the student completing the assignment.

For example:

"My name is [your full name], and I'm a student of Communication & Public Speaking at Unify Creator Academy. I'm about to have a conversation with [the person's first name], and this conversation is part of my Module 1, Week 2 practical assignment."

Then introduce the person you're speaking with, if they are comfortable with that, and begin your conversation naturally.

You do not need to make the introduction sound formal. Simply make sure your name is clearly stated at the beginning.

YOUR TASK

During the conversation, demonstrate the following:

1. Ask questions that encourage the person to open up.

Ask thoughtful questions that encourage the person to explain their experiences, opinions, ideas, or feelings rather than relying only on yes-or-no questions.

2. Practise active listening.

Allow the person to finish speaking before you respond. Avoid constantly interrupting, rushing to give advice, or making the conversation about yourself.

3. Ask follow-up questions.

Pay attention to the person's answers and ask relevant follow-up questions based on what they say.

4. Practise clarification and reflective listening.

At an appropriate point, explain what you understand the person to mean and allow them to correct you if necessary.

For example:

"So, if I understand you correctly, what you're saying is..."

5. Read conversational cues.

Pay attention to the person's tone, pauses, expressions, and level of engagement. Notice when they seem interested, uncomfortable, confused, or reluctant to continue discussing something, and respond appropriately.

6. Build rapport and adapt.

Make the conversation comfortable and natural. Demonstrate genuine interest, and adjust your approach when necessary.

RECORDING REQUIREMENTS

You may submit either:

- A video recording: Record the conversation while ensuring that the interaction can be heard clearly.
- An audio recording: Record the conversation using your phone's voice recorder or another suitable audio-recording app.

Your recording must contain at least 3 minutes of usable conversation taken from your 5-10-minute interaction.

If you submit audio, make sure your voice and the other person's voice can be distinguished clearly. Your introduction at the beginning must identify you as the student completing the assignment.

The recording must capture a genuine conversation, including your questions, the other person's responses, your listening, and your follow-up questions.

Important: Obtain the other person's consent before recording. Never secretly record anyone, and do not pressure anyone to participate or reveal sensitive personal information.

PART 2: THE PUBLIC SPEAKING AND INFLUENCE CHALLENGE

Listening is only one side of communication. You must also demonstrate that you can express an idea clearly, hold an audience's attention, and communicate with a purpose.

YOUR TASK

Choose ONE topic from the options below:

- Why young people should learn a skill before graduating.
- Why people should stop comparing their lives to others on social media.
- Why effective communication is an important life skill.
- Why students should take their personal development seriously.
- Why people should learn to listen before responding.
- Why consistency matters more than motivation.
- Why everyone should learn how to manage their money.
- Why people should be more intentional about the content they consume.
- Why young people should build a personal brand.
- A topic of your choice, provided it is appropriate and gives you a genuine position to defend.

YOUR MISSION

Deliver a 2-3-minute persuasive speech in which you try to convince your audience to understand, believe, or do something.

You may submit your speech as either a video or an audio recording.

Before delivering your speech, introduce yourself:

"My name is [your full name], and I'm a student of Communication & Public Speaking at Unify Creator Academy. This is my Module 1, Week 2 persuasive speech."

Then proceed with your speech.

YOUR SPEECH MUST DEMONSTRATE:

1. Clarity: Your audience should understand exactly what you are trying to communicate.

2. A strong opening: Begin with a question, bold statement, relatable situation, or surprising observation that makes people interested in listening.

3. Logical organisation: Present your ideas in an order that makes sense. Explain your position, support it with reasons or examples, and conclude clearly.

4. Conciseness: Avoid unnecessary repetition, irrelevant stories, and excessive introductions.

5. Influence: Give your audience reasons to consider your position. Support your argument with explanations, examples, evidence, or relatable experiences.

6. Intentional delivery: Pay attention to your tone, pace, pauses, and choice of words. If you submit video, also pay attention to your posture, facial expressions, and eye contact with the camera.

7. A meaningful conclusion: End by reinforcing your message or giving your audience a clear action to take.

THE EXTRA CHALLENGE

Do not read your speech word for word from a script.

You may prepare notes and practise beforehand, but your delivery should sound natural rather than like someone reading an essay aloud.

If you submit audio, focus on your voice, pace, pauses, emphasis, and ability to keep the listener engaged.

If you submit video, ensure that your visual delivery supports your message.

Your job is to make your audience understand your message and give them a reason to care.

PART 3: THE SELF-REVIEW CHALLENGE

After completing both recordings, listen to or watch them critically.

For the conversation, assess whether you interrupted, asked relevant follow-up questions, listened carefully, and responded to what the other person actually said.

For the speech, assess whether your message was clear, whether you repeated yourself, whether your opening held attention, and whether your delivery helped communicate your message.

Identify at least one specific thing you would improve in each performance.

You do not need to submit a written review. The purpose is to assess your performance honestly and recognise where you need to improve.

SUBMISSION REQUIREMENTS

Submit TWO recordings:

RECORDING 1 — THE CONVERSATION

- Duration: Approximately 5-10 minutes for the full conversation.
- Submit at least 3 minutes of usable conversation.
- Format: Video or audio.
- Must begin with your name and a brief introduction.
- Must demonstrate genuine listening and conversational skills.

RECORDING 2 — THE PERSUASIVE SPEECH

- Duration: 2-3 minutes.
- Format: Video or audio.
- Must begin with your name and a brief introduction.
- Must demonstrate clear, organised, persuasive communication.

You may submit both recordings in the same format or use different formats for each.

HOW TO SUBMIT USING GOOGLE DRIVE ON YOUR PHONE

Step 1: Create a folder

1. Open the Google Drive app.
2. Tap the + button.
3. Select New folder.
4. Name the folder: "UCA - Module 1 Week 2 - Communication Assignment - Your Name"
5. Open the folder.

Step 2: Upload your recordings

1. Tap the + button.
2. Select Upload.
3. Locate your conversation recording and upload it.
4. Repeat the process for your persuasive speech.
5. Wait until both files finish uploading.

If you used your phone's voice recorder, locate the saved audio file and upload it just as you would a video.

Step 3: Change the folder's access settings

1. Return to your Google Drive folder.
2. Tap the three dots beside the folder's name.
3. Select Share or Manage access.
4. Under General access, change Restricted to Anyone with the link, if available.
5. Set the permission to Viewer.
6. Save your changes.

This allows your examiner to access the recordings without needing your Google account login.

Step 4: Submit your link

1. Tap the three dots beside the folder.
2. Select Share, then Copy link.
3. Open the UCA Assignment Portal.
4. Paste the folder link into the appropriate submission field.
5. Submit your assignment.

Step 5: Test your link

Before submitting, check that both recordings can be accessed.

If you have difficulty, search YouTube for a tutorial on uploading audio recordings to Google Drive using an Android phone or changing Google Drive folder permissions.

You may also ask a classmate, peer, or facilitator for help.

Do not wait until the deadline to discover that your link does not work.

SUBMISSION DEADLINE

Assignment opens: Wednesday.

Deadline: Friday, 11:59 PM.

Both recordings must be submitted before the deadline.
assignment.requirements:
HOW YOUR ASSIGNMENT WILL BE ASSESSED

CONVERSATION

- Active listening.
- Quality of questions and follow-up questions.
- Understanding and clarification.
- Recognition of conversational cues.
- Rapport and adaptability.

PUBLIC SPEAKING AND INFLUENCE

- Clarity of message.
- Logical organisation.
- Conciseness.
- Persuasiveness.
- Vocal delivery and audience engagement.
- Natural communication.

SUBMISSION

- Both recordings are provided.
- Your name is clearly stated at the beginning of each recording.
- The recordings meet the required durations and demonstrate the skills being assessed.
- The Google Drive link works and provides access to both files.

FINAL CHALLENGE

Can you listen to another person without constantly preparing your response?

Can you ask questions that make a conversation more meaningful?

Can you read the situation and respond appropriately?

And when it is your turn to speak, can you communicate an idea clearly enough to influence another person's thinking?

Listen to understand. Speak to be understood. Communicate to make an impact.

That is your challenge.
